newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich endorses U.S. refuge for Swiss guard.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich endorses U.S. refuge for Swiss guard.

text.p: House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich on Wednesday endorsed special legislation to grant legal residency in the United States for a young Swiss bank guard who tried to stop Nazi-era bank records from being shredded.
Christophe Meili, 29, told U.S. lawmakers last month he and his family had received threats since he exposed the order to shred the Holocaust-era documents.

"The heroic efforts of this young man deserve commendation, not prosecution, and I will do everything in my power to ensure that this legislation is quickly brought to the House floor and approved," Gingrich, a Georgia Republican, said in a statement.
Gingrich also called for an end to what he called "a thick veil of Swiss bank secrecy," surrounding the issue of unclaimed assets of Holocaust victims still in Swiss banks.
The legislation giving him permanent residency status cleared the Senate last month and passed a House Judiciary subcommittee Tuesday. It will now go to the full committee and then to the full House.

"A thick veil of Swiss bank secrecy has covered this entire affair for too long. It's time to uncover what really happened to the hundreds of millions of dollars of Jewish gold and assets that disappeared in Switzerland following World War Two," Gingrich said.
Congress rarely passes private relief legislation but in this case he would not have qualified for legal immigrant status under normal rules.

Meili was a student and night security guard at the Union Bank of Switzerland when he stumbled on the carts of Holocaust-era documents waiting for the shredder. Swiss authorities have not closed their case against him for violating the nation's strict bank secrecy laws because he showed the documents to members of the Swiss Jewish community.

A commission headed by former Federal Reserve Board chairman Paul Volcker and set up last year by the World Jewish Restitution Organisation and Swiss banks is expected to name soon the first banks whose records will be audited in its probe of unclaimed assets of Holocaust victims.
